questions.explanation_english: The Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) prescribes a standard 200-point model roster for direct recruitment on an All-India basis by open competition. questions.question_english: The RPwD Act, 2016 specifies certain conditions under which a person with disability might be subjected to differential treatment. Which of the following represents a legally valid ground for such action under the Act?
options_english: When it significantly reduces the operational and administrative burden on management
When shown as a proportionate means to achieve a legitimate aim
When the parent or legal guardian of the child explicitly consents to it
When the institution demonstrates a complete lack of adequate financial resources
questions.explanation_english: Section 3(1) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 strictly prohibits discrimination against any person with disability on the ground of disability, unless it is shown that the impugned act or omission is a 'proportionate means of achieving a legitimate aim'. The law imposes a rigorous proportionality test, meaning differential treatment cannot be excused on grounds of administrative convenience, financial incapacity, institutional preferences, or parental consent. Any departure from non-discrimination must serve a legitimate statutory purpose and must be strictly proportionate, ensuring that arbitrary distinctions violate Article 14 of the Constitution.
questions.explanation_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 की धारा 3(1) दिव्यांगता के आधार पर किसी भी प्रकार के भेदभाव को पूरी तरह प्रतिबंधित करती है, जब तक कि यह सिद्ध न कर दिया जाए कि ऐसा कृत्य या चूक 'किसी वैध उद्देश्य को प्राप्त करने का एक आनुपातिक साधन' (proportionate means of achieving a legitimate aim) है। यह कानून कड़े आनुपातिकता परीक्षण को लागू करता है; अतः प्रशासनिक सुविधा, वित्तीय तंगी या अभिभावकों की सहमति को विभेदकारी व्यवहार का कानूनी आधार नहीं बनाया जा सकता। किसी भी भिन्न व्यवहार को वैध कानूनी उद्देश्य की कसौटी पर खरा उतरना होगा ताकि संविधान के अनुच्छेद 14 का उल्लंघन न हो।
questions.topic: Constitutional Provisions for PwBD, EWS, SC, ST, and Disadvantaged Groups
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) When shown as a proportionate means to achieve a legitimate aim

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: achieve a legitimate aim The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act of 2016 permits differential treatment of a person with a disability only under specific legal exceptions. Such treatment is valid solely when it can be objectively demonstrated that the action or distinction constitutes a proportionate means of achieving a legitimate aim, thereby protecting individuals against arbitrary administrative discrimination or convenience-based exclusions.

questions.question_english: What is the fundamental difference between a "person with disability" and a "person with benchmark disability" as defined in the RPwD Act, 2016?
options_english: Benchmark disability requires at least 40% certified specified disability, while disability covers any long-term impairment
Benchmark disability applies strictly to physical impairments, whereas disability covers all physical and mental impairments
Benchmark disability applies exclusively to adult citizens, whereas general disability applies to both children and adults
Benchmark disability requires a mandatory income certificate, whereas general disability classification requires no financial proof
questions.explanation_english:
The RPwD Act, 2016 maintains a vital distinction between general disability and benchmark disability:
1. Section 2(s) defines a 'person with disability' as a person with long-term physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory impairment which, in interaction with barriers, hinders their full and effective participation in society equally with others.
2. Section 2(r) defines a 'person with benchmark disability' as a person with not less than forty percent (40%) of a specified disability (as certified by a certifying medical authority), or a person with disability where specified disability has not been defined in measurable terms.
A certified benchmark disability (minimum 40%) is a statutory prerequisite to claim reservations in higher educational institutions (Section 32, minimum 5%), government employment (Section 34, minimum 4%), free education up to 18 years of age (Section 31), and priority in government welfare schemes.
questions.explanation_hindi:
RPwD अधिनियम, 2016 में सामान्य दिव्यांगता और बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगता के बीच एक स्पष्ट विधिक अंतर है:
1. धारा 2(s) के तहत 'दिव्यांग व्यक्ति' वह है जिसे कोई भी दीर्घकालिक शारीरिक, मानसिक, बौद्धिक या संवेदी दुर्बलता हो, जो विभिन्न बाधाओं के साथ परस्पर क्रिया में समाज में उसके पूर्ण और समान समावेशन में रुकावट डालती है।
2. धारा 2(r) के तहत 'बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगता वाला व्यक्ति' वह है जिसके पास सक्षम चिकित्सा प्राधिकारी द्वारा जारी कम से कम 40% (चालीस प्रतिशत) विनिर्दिष्ट दिव्यांगता का प्रमाणपत्र हो।
यह न्यूनतम 40% की अर्हता उच्च शिक्षण संस्थानों में आरक्षण (धारा 32 के तहत न्यूनतम 5%), सरकारी नौकरियों में आरक्षण (धारा 34 के तहत न्यूनतम 4%) तथा 6 से 18 वर्ष तक निःशुल्क शिक्षा (धारा 31) जैसी सकारात्मक कार्रवाइयों का लाभ उठाने के लिए अनिवार्य है।

questions.question_english: The determination of whether a class of citizens is "socially and educationally backward" under Article 15(4) relies primarily on:
options_english: Financial and income criteria considered alone
Academic and educational backwardness alone
Social and educational backwardness
Occupational status and economic standing alone
questions.explanation_english: The determination of backwardness for affirmative action benefits under Article 15(4) must be based on both social and educational backwardness. The constitutional text explicitly specifies 'socially and educationally backward classes'. In landmark rulings such as M.R. Balaji v. State of Mysore (1963) and the 9-judge Constitution Bench in Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992), the Supreme Court affirmed that backwardness contemplated under Article 15(4) is composite: it must be primarily social, and that social backwardness leads to educational backwardness. Economic criteria or poverty alone cannot be the sole basis of classification under Article 15(4) (unlike the later 103rd Amendment inserting Article 15(6) for EWS). Therefore, the test under Article 15(4) strictly requires dual social and educational backwardness.
questions.explanation_hindi: अनुच्छेद 15(4) के तहत आरक्षण और सकारात्मक लाभों के लिए पिछड़ेपन का निर्धारण सामाजिक और शैक्षणिक दोनों पिछड़ेपन पर आधारित होना चाहिए। संवैधानिक मूल पाठ में स्पष्ट रूप से 'सामाजिक और शैक्षणिक रूप से पिछड़े वर्ग' (SEBCs) शब्द का उपयोग किया गया है। 'एम.आर. बालाजी बनाम मैसूर राज्य (1963)' तथा 'इंद्रा साहनी बनाम भारत संघ (1992)' (9-न्यायाधीशों की संविधान पीठ) में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने यह स्थापित किया कि अनुच्छेद 15(4) के अंतर्गत पिछड़ापन मुख्य रूप से सामाजिक होना चाहिए, जो आगे चलकर शैक्षणिक पिछड़ेपन को जन्म देता है। केवल आर्थिक गरीबी या आय का स्तर अनुच्छेद 15(4) के तहत वर्गीकरण का एकमात्र आधार नहीं हो सकता (आर्थिक रूप से कमजोर वर्गों के लिए बाद में 103वें संशोधन द्वारा अनुच्छेद 15(6) जोड़ा गया)। अतः अनुच्छेद 15(4) के तहत सामाजिक और शैक्षणिक पिछड़ापन दोनों ही अनिवार्य आधार हैं।

key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Social and educational backwardness

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The determination of backwardness for the purpose of granting affirmative action benefits under Article 15(4) must be based primarily on social and educational backwardness. Economic criteria alone cannot be the sole basis for classification under this specific clause, as established by constitutional text and settled jurisprudence of the Supreme Court of India.

questions.question_english: During the probationary period, what is the prescribed government policy regarding the extension of probation for reserved category teachers who fail to attain the required performance standard for confirmation?
options_english: Probation cannot be extended and they must be confirmed in service automatically
Their services must be terminated immediately without granting any extension
Probation may be extended with special training opportunities provided
They are demoted to a lower administrative post permanently without appeal
questions.explanation_english: Under Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) guidelines (including OM No. 28020/1/2010-Estt.(C) and Master Circular on Probation), the government has established protective measures for probationers from reserved communities (SC/ST/OBC/PwBD). If an appointee belonging to a reserved category fails to meet the expected performance standard during the normal probation period, their service is not summarily terminated. Instead, the appointing authority extends their probation period and provides constructive feedback, targeted mentoring, and special training opportunities. This policy ensures affirmative institutional support to help the employee overcome identified deficiencies and achieve the required level of professional competence prior to final confirmation.
questions.explanation_hindi: कार्मिक एवं प्रशिक्षण विभाग (DoPT) के दिशा-निर्देशों एवं प्रोबेशन पर जारी मास्टर सर्कुलर के अनुसार, आरक्षित वर्ग (SC/ST/OBC/PwBD) के कर्मचारियों के लिए विशेष उपचारात्मक नीति निर्धारित की गई है। यदि परिवीक्षा (प्रोबेशन) अवधि के दौरान आरक्षित वर्ग का कोई शिक्षक अपेक्षित कार्य-दक्षता या मानक प्राप्त करने में विफल रहता है, तो उसकी सेवाएं तत्काल समाप्त नहीं की जाती हैं। इसके बजाय, नियुक्ति प्राधिकारी द्वारा उसकी परिवीक्षा अवधि को बढ़ाया जा सकता है और इस विस्तारित अवधि के दौरान उसे अपनी कमियों को दूर करने के लिए विशेष प्रशिक्षण के अवसर, मार्गदर्शन और उपचारात्मक कोचिंग प्रदान की जाती है ताकि वह स्थायीकरण हेतु आवश्यक दक्षता प्राप्त कर सके। अतः विकल्प C सही उत्तर है।

questions.explanation_english: Article 338 of the Constitution of India establishes the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC). Under Article 338(5), the Commission has the duty to investigate and monitor all matters relating to the safeguards provided for the Scheduled Castes under the Constitution or any other law, and to inquire into specific complaints with respect to the deprivation of rights and safeguards of the Scheduled Castes. Under Article 338(8), while investigating any matter or inquiring into any complaint relating to denial of promotion, harassment, or roster tampering involving an SC employee, the Commission is vested with all the powers of a Civil Court trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. This includes summoning and enforcing the attendance of witnesses, examining them on oath, discovery and production of documents, and requisitioning public records from any school or education directorate.

questions.question_english: A parent of a child admitted under the Economically Weaker Section (EWS) quota in a private unaided recognized school submits a written complaint to the Principal, stating that the school is demanding fees for textbooks and uniform contrary to RTE rules. What is the legally correct and mandatory response of the Principal?
options_english: Reject the complaint stating books and uniforms are never free in private schools
Provide books and uniforms free, seeking reimbursement from the State
Advise the parent to transfer the child to a state school if unable to pay costs
Forward the complaint to the local police department for extortion inquiry
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 12(1)(c) and Section 12(2) of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, private unaided recognized schools admitting children under the 25% EWS and Disadvantaged Group (DG) quota must provide free and compulsory elementary education. High Courts across the country, notably the Delhi High Court in landmark rulings (such as 'Justice for All v. Govt. of NCT of Delhi' and 'Federation of Public Schools v. GNCTD'), have conclusively held that 'free education' is not restricted merely to tuition fees. It includes the mandatory provision of free textbooks, writing materials, and school uniforms, as financial barriers in purchasing these essential materials prevent underprivileged children from participating equally in school. The school is legally prohibited from charging any money from the parents for these entitlements; instead, the school management must supply them free of cost and seek per-child statutory reimbursement from the State Government under Section 12(2).

questions.question_english: The constitutional rule that total reservation in public employment under Article 16(4) should ordinarily not exceed the 50% ceiling limit was authoritatively established by a nine-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in which landmark judgment?
options_english: Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India (1980)
M. Nagaraj v. Union of India (2006)
Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992)
Jarnail Singh v. L.N. Gupta (2018)
questions.explanation_english:
The 50% ceiling rule on reservations in public employment was authoritatively established by a nine-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court of India in Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992 Supp (3) SCC 217), popularly known as the Mandal Commission Case.

Key principles established in Indra Sawhney:
1. 50% Ceiling Limit: Reservation under Article 16(4) must not exceed 50% of appointments in any year, except in extraordinary situations inherent to far-flung and remote areas where people are cut off from the national mainstream.
2. Exclusion of Creamy Layer: The affluent/advanced sections among Other Backward Classes (OBCs) must be excluded from the purview of affirmative action.
3. Scope Confined to Direct Recruitment: Article 16(4) does not permit reservation in promotions (which subsequently led to the 77th and 85th Constitutional Amendments adding Article 16(4A)).
4. Vertical vs Horizontal Reservation: Quotas for SC, ST, and OBC are vertical reservations, whereas reservations for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD), women, and ex-servicemen are horizontal reservations that cut across vertical categories under Article 16(1).
questions.explanation_hindi:
सार्वजनिक रोजगार में आरक्षण पर 50% की अधिकतम सीमा का संवैधानिक सिद्धांत सर्वोच्च न्यायालय की नौ-न्यायाधीशों की संविधान पीठ द्वारा 'इंद्रा साहनी बनाम भारत संघ (1992)' (जिसे लोकप्रिय रूप से मंडल कमीशन केस कहा जाता है) में प्रामाणिक रूप से स्थापित किया गया था।

इंद्रा साहनी मामले के प्रमुख सिद्धांत:
1. 50% की अधिकतम सीमा: अनुच्छेद 16(4) के तहत कुल आरक्षण किसी भी वर्ष में 50% से अधिक नहीं होना चाहिए, सिवाय अत्यंत असाधारण और दूर-दराज के विषम भौगोलिक क्षेत्रों की परिस्थितियों को छोड़कर।
2. क्रीमी लेयर (मलाईदार परत) का अपवर्जन: अन्य पिछड़ा वर्ग (OBC) के भीतर सामाजिक एवं आर्थिक रूप से संपन्न व्यक्तियों को आरक्षण के लाभ से बाहर रखा जाना चाहिए।
3. पदोन्नति में आरक्षण नहीं: न्यायालय ने माना कि अनुच्छेद 16(4) पदोन्नति में आरक्षण की अनुमति नहीं देता (जिसके कारण बाद में संसद को 77वां और 85वां संविधान संशोधन लाकर अनुच्छेद 16(4A) जोड़ना पड़ा)।
4. लंबवत (वर्टिकल) बनाम क्षैतिज (हॉरिजॉन्टल) आरक्षण: SC, ST और OBC आरक्षण लंबवत श्रेणियां हैं, जबकि दिव्यांगजन (PwBD), भूतपूर्व सैनिक और महिलाओं के लिए आरक्षण क्षैतिज आरक्षण है, जो अनुच्छेद 16(1) के तहत सभी लंबवत श्रेणियों में अंतर्निहित होता है।

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 4 of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 (POSH Act) read with CBSE, UGC, and Ministry of Education safety regulations, every educational institution employing 10 or more employees must constitute an 'Internal Complaints Committee' (ICC). The ICC is a specialized quasi-judicial committee headed by a senior woman presiding officer, with members from non-governmental organizations or legal backgrounds. When a female student or staff member with a disability files a complaint of sexual harassment, the ICC has primary statutory jurisdiction to conduct a formal, confidential inquiry while observing principles of natural justice and providing reasonable accommodations (e.g., sign language interpreter or scribe). If the student is a minor, the POCSO Act, 2012 provisions for mandatory reporting to Special Juvenile Police Unit (SJPU) operate simultaneously.

Exemptions from standard educational curricula
Mandatory separate schooling
Reasonable accommodation
questions.explanation_english: Section 3 of the RPwD Act, 2016 mandates equality and non-discrimination for persons with disabilities. Subsection (5) of Section 3 specifically provides that the appropriate Government shall take necessary steps to ensure reasonable accommodation for persons with disabilities. 'Reasonable accommodation' is defined under Section 2(y) as necessary and appropriate modification and adjustments, not imposing a disproportionate or undue burden in a particular case, to ensure to persons with disabilities the enjoyment or exercise of rights equally with others. This concept serves as the foundational legal tool to achieve substantive equality (as opposed to mere formal equality) under Articles 14 and 15 of the Constitution of India.

questions.question_english: Which of the following constitutional articles works in tandem with Article 15(4) to permit the reservation of seats for SC, ST, and SEBC candidates in educational institutions?
options_english: Article 29(2)
Article 19(1)(g)
Article 30(1)

questions.explanation_english: Article 15(4) operates in direct conjunction with Article 29(2) of the Indian Constitution. Article 29(2) guarantees that no citizen shall be denied admission into any educational institution maintained by the State or receiving aid out of State funds on grounds only of religion, race, caste, language, or any of them. The opening non-obstante clause of Article 15(4)—'Nothing in this article or in clause (2) of article 29 shall prevent the State from making any special provision...'—specifically creates an exception to Article 29(2). This ensures that reserving seats, waiving fees, or lowering admission criteria for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Socially and Educationally Backward Classes in government or state-aided institutions cannot be challenged as prohibited caste-based discrimination under Article 29(2).
questions.explanation_hindi: अनुच्छेद 15(4) भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 29(2) के साथ घनिष्ठ संबंध में कार्य करता है। अनुच्छेद 29(2) प्रत्येक नागरिक को यह मौलिक गारंटी देता है कि राज्य द्वारा पोषित या राज्य निधि से सहायता प्राप्त किसी भी शैक्षणिक संस्थान में प्रवेश से केवल धर्म, मूलवंश, जाति, भाषा या इनमें से किसी के आधार पर वंचित नहीं किया जाएगा। अनुच्छेद 15(4) की शुरुआत एक गैर-अवरोधक खंड (non-obstante clause) से होती है: 'इस अनुच्छेद की या अनुच्छेद 29 के खंड (2) की कोई बात राज्य को... विशेष उपबंध करने से निवारित नहीं करेगी'। यह उपबंध अनुच्छेद 29(2) के सामान्य गैर-भेदभाव नियम का एक प्रत्यक्ष संवैधानिक अपवाद निर्मित करता है, जिससे राज्य द्वारा संचालित या सहायता प्राप्त स्कूलों और कॉलेजों में SC, ST और SEBC के लिए सीटों का आरक्षण अनुच्छेद 29(2) का उल्लंघन नहीं माना जाता।

questions.question_english: If a reserved vacancy in a teaching or administrative post cannot be filled due to the non-availability of an eligible candidate from the respective reserved category, the formal process of lifting the reservation restriction to fill it with an unreserved candidate is termed as:
options_english: Derecognition
De-reservation
Generalization

questions.explanation_english: In government service and educational administration, the formal procedure of removing the reservation tag from a reserved vacancy to enable the appointment of an unreserved/general candidate is officially termed 'De-reservation' (वि-आरक्षण). Under current DoPT rules and government policy, there is a general ban on de-reservation in direct recruitment posts; unfilled reserved vacancies must ordinarily be re-advertised and carried forward as 'backlog vacancies'. De-reservation in direct recruitment is permissible only in exceptionally rare and unavoidable circumstances in public interest, requiring prior concurrence from the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) and consultation with the relevant National Commission (NCSC, NCST, or NCBC). In promotion cadres, de-reservation follows a rigorous statutory approval mechanism to protect reserved quotas.

questions.question_english: What is the maximum ceiling of reservation permitted for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) in admissions to educational institutions and public appointments under Articles 15(6) and 16(6) of the Constitution?
questions.explanation_english:
Under the express text of Article 15(6) and Article 16(6) introduced by the 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019, the reservation permitted for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) is subject to a strict statutory cap:

- Article 15(6)(b) states that reservations in educational institutions 'would be in addition to the existing reservations and subject to a maximum of ten per cent of the total seats in each category.'
- Article 16(6) provides that reservation in appointments or posts 'shall be in addition to the existing reservation and subject to a maximum of ten per cent of the posts in each category.'

This 10% quota operates in addition to the existing reservations for Scheduled Castes (15%), Scheduled Tribes (7.5%), and Other Backward Classes (27%), taking total vertical reservations under central laws up to 59.5%.
questions.explanation_hindi:

questions.question_english: What is the fundamental difference in the scope and application between Article 15(4) and Article 16(4) of the Constitution of India?
options_english: Article 15(4) deals exclusively with economic backwardness, whereas Article 16(4) pertains strictly to social backwardness
Article 15(4) enables special provisions including admission to educational institutions, whereas Article 16(4) provides for reservation in public employment
Article 15(4) applies exclusively to religious minorities, while Article 16(4) applies solely to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
Article 15(4) mandates a rigid 50% reservation ceiling, whereas Article 16(4) prescribes no ceiling limit on quotas
questions.explanation_english:
The fundamental distinction between Article 15(4) and Article 16(4) of the Constitution of India lies in their distinct functional domains:

1. Article 15(4): Inserted by the First Constitutional Amendment Act of 1951 (following the landmark State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan case), Article 15(4) is a general enabling provision. It empowers the State to make 'special provisions for the advancement of any socially and educationally backward classes of citizens or for the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes.' In educational governance and administrative practice, this provides the constitutional authority for affirmative action in education, including fee concessions, age relaxations, and reserved quotas in admission to state-run or state-aided colleges and universities.

2. Article 16(4): Positioned within the framework of equality of opportunity in public employment, Article 16(4) specifically empowers the State to make 'any provision for the reservation of appointments or posts in favour of any backward class of citizens which, in the opinion of the State, is not adequately represented in the services under the State.' Its scope is confined strictly to public services, recruitment rosters, and employment under the Union or State Governments, including appointments in government school systems.

Therefore, while Article 15(4) governs educational access and general socio-economic advancement, Article 16(4) governs appointments and recruitment in government posts and public employment.
questions.explanation_hindi:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 15(4) और अनुच्छेद 16(4) के बीच का मूलभूत अंतर उनके कार्यक्षेत्र (डोमेन) में निहित है:

1. अनुच्छेद 15(4): प्रथम संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 1951 द्वारा (मद्रास राज्य बनाम चंपकम दोराइराजन मामले के उपरांत) जोड़ा गया अनुच्छेद 15(4) एक सामान्य समर्थकारी प्रावधान है। यह राज्य को 'सामाजिक और शैक्षिक दृष्टि से पिछड़े नागरिकों के किन्हीं वर्गों की उन्नति के लिए या अनुसूचित जातियों और अनुसूचित जनजातियों के लिए कोई विशेष उपबंध' करने की शक्ति देता है। इसके तहत शिक्षण संस्थानों (स्कूलों, महाविद्यालयों और विश्वविद्यालयों) में प्रवेश, शुल्क में रियायत तथा विशेष योजनाओं का प्रावधान किया जाता है।

2. अनुच्छेद 16(4): यह सार्वजनिक रोजगार में अवसर की समानता के दायरे में कार्य करता है। यह विशेष रूप से राज्य को 'नागरिकों के किसी पिछड़े वर्ग के पक्ष में, जिनका राज्य की राय में राज्य के अधीन सेवाओं में पर्याप्त प्रतिनिधित्व नहीं है, नियुक्तियों या पदों के आरक्षण के लिए उपबंध' करने का अधिकार प्रदान करता है। इसका दायरा पूरी तरह से सरकारी सेवाओं और सार्वजनिक रोजगार में पदों के आरक्षण तक सीमित है।

अतः अनुच्छेद 15(4) का संबंध मुख्य रूप से शैक्षणिक प्रवेश और सामान्य सामाजिक उत्थान से है, जबकि अनुच्छेद 16(4) का संबंध सार्वजनिक रोजगार और सरकारी नौकरियों में नियुक्तियों से है।

questions.explanation_english: Under the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) Office Memorandum No. 36039/1/2019-Estt (Res) dated 31st January 2019, issued pursuant to the Constitution (One Hundred and Third Amendment) Act, 2019, the definition of "Family" for the purpose of determining EWS eligibility is strictly specified in Paragraph 4.1. Consequently, the income and assets of adult children (aged 18 and above) or adult siblings (aged 18 and above), as well as grandparents, uncles, or other extended relatives, are excluded from the family income/asset calculation. questions.explanation_english: Prior to 2005, Article 15(4) enabled reservations and special provisions primarily in government-run and state-aided educational institutions. In landmark decisions like T.M.A. Pai Foundation (2002) and P.A. Inamdar v. State of Maharashtra (2005), the Supreme Court ruled that the State could not impose reservation quotas on private unaided educational institutions, holding that such restrictions violated the fundamental right to carry on an occupation under Article 19(1)(g). To bridge this critical constitutional gap and ensure that private unaided professional colleges and schools share the burden of affirmative action, Parliament enacted the 93rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2005, inserting Article 15(5). This clause specifically empowered the State to mandate reservations in educational institutions, including private unaided institutions, other than minority educational institutions.
questions.explanation_hindi: वर्ष 2005 से पहले, अनुच्छेद 15(4) मुख्य रूप से सरकारी और राज्य-सहायता प्राप्त शैक्षणिक संस्थानों में ही आरक्षण और विशेष प्रावधान करने में सक्षम था। सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने 'टी.एम.ए. पाई फाउंडेशन (2002)' तथा 'पी.ए. इनामदार बनाम महाराष्ट्र राज्य (2005)' के निर्णयों में स्पष्ट किया कि राज्य निजी गैर-सहायता प्राप्त शैक्षणिक संस्थानों पर आरक्षण या कोटा नहीं थोप सकता, क्योंकि यह अनुच्छेद 19(1)(g) के तहत उनके व्यवसाय के मौलिक अधिकार का हनन करता है। इस गंभीर संवैधानिक शून्यता को भरने और निजी गैर-सहायता प्राप्त संस्थानों (विशेष रूप से उच्च व व्यावसायिक शिक्षण संस्थानों) में भी वंचित वर्गों को प्रतिनिधित्व दिलाने के लिए संसद ने 93वें संविधान संशोधन द्वारा अनुच्छेद 15(5) जोड़ा। इसने निजी गैर-सहायता प्राप्त संस्थानों में भी आरक्षण लागू करने की राज्य की शक्ति का मार्ग प्रशस्त किया।

questions.question_english: Within the administrative framework of school education (such as the Directorate of Education, GNCTD), supplying free textbooks, uniforms, and learning materials to students belonging to weaker sections represents an administrative implementation of which Constitutional Article?
options_english: Article 44
Article 46
Article 50

questions.explanation_english:
Article 46 of the Constitution of India explicitly mandates that the State shall promote with special care the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections of the people, especially Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, and protect them from social injustice.

In administrative practice, educational directorates across States and Union Territories—such as the Directorate of Education, Government of NCT of Delhi (GNCTD)—translate this constitutional directive into actionable public welfare schemes. Initiatives providing free textbooks, uniforms, stationery, mid-day meals, and pre-matric/post-matric stipends to students from disadvantaged groups and economically weaker sections are designed to remove economic barriers preventing retention and completion of schooling.

Other options are unrelated: Article 44 pertains to a Uniform Civil Code; Article 50 deals with the separation of the judiciary from the executive; and Article 350A concerns facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage.
questions.explanation_hindi:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 46 यह अनिवार्य करता है कि राज्य समाज के कमजोर वर्गों, विशेषकर अनुसूचित जातियों और अनुसूचित जनजातियों के शैक्षणिक और आर्थिक हितों की विशेष सावधानी से अभिवृद्धि करेगा तथा उन्हें सामाजिक अन्याय से बचाएगा।

प्रशासनिक स्तर पर, राज्यों और केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों के शिक्षा निदेशालय (जैसे दिल्ली सरकार का शिक्षा निदेशालय - GNCTD) इस संवैधानिक निर्देश को धरातल पर उतारने के लिए विभिन्न कल्याणकारी योजनाएं संचालित करते हैं। वंचित और कमजोर वर्गों के बच्चों को निःशुल्क पाठ्यपुस्तकें, स्कूल वर्दी, लेखन सामग्री तथा छात्रवृत्तियां प्रदान करना अनुच्छेद 46 के आदर्शों का सीधा प्रशासनिक प्रकटीकरण है, ताकि गरीबी के कारण कोई भी बच्चा शिक्षा से वंचित न रहे।

अन्य विकल्प असंगत हैं: अनुच्छेद 44 समान नागरिक संहिता से संबंधित है; अनुच्छेद 50 कार्यपालिका से न्यायपालिका के पृथक्करण से संबंधित है; और अनुच्छेद 350A प्राथमिक स्तर पर मातृभाषा में शिक्षा की सुविधाओं से संबंधित है।
